scenarios.name: approval_allow_kernel
scenarios.summary: A WRITE tool in `ask` mode; a scripted human approves via Commands.resolve_approval; the write happens.

scenarios.name: approval_allow_web_dom
scenarios.summary: Approval flow through the real UI — the jsdom client receives approval.required, clicks the approve button, the write lands, the turn completes.

scenarios.name: approval_deny_no_approver_kernel
scenarios.summary: Same WRITE in `ask` mode with no interactive subscriber on the bus — must be denied immediately (fail closed) and the model told.

scenarios.name: ask_user_answered
scenarios.summary: The browser renders a structured question, submits an answer, and reloads both durable facts.

scenarios.name: ask_user_headless
scenarios.summary: Headless ask_user fails promptly with a model-visible error so the turn can continue.

scenarios.name: daemon_restart_web_dom
scenarios.summary: Two turns through the real client, then the daemon is stopped and started again on the same workspace — the client must land on the same conversation without any click, and no empty session may be created by the restart or the page load.

scenarios.name: jail_blocks_traversal_kernel
scenarios.summary: Workspace jail — a read and a write outside the workspace are denied by policy even in allow mode; nothing is read or written; the model is told why.

scenarios.name: job_finishes_between_turns
scenarios.summary: A background job emits durable lifecycle records and its completion is announced to the next turn.

scenarios.name: mcp_echo_kernel
scenarios.summary: An MCP tool (stdio echo fixture) executes through the gate; regression for review Addendum A.2 as a scenario.

scenarios.name: memory_remember_search_kernel
scenarios.summary: remember → (same session) search_memory finds the fact; regression for review Addendum A.1 as a scenario.

scenarios.name: memory_remember_web_dom
scenarios.summary: Memory through the real client — remember in turn one, search_memory in turn two; both tool cards render and the found fact is shown.

scenarios.name: plain_answer_kernel
scenarios.summary: A streamed text answer through Commands.submit_turn; transcript persisted and identical after a restart.

scenarios.name: plain_answer_web
scenarios.summary: The shipped browser client (jsdom) sends a prompt, receives the kernel's named SSE events and renders the answer.

scenarios.name: present_artifact
scenarios.summary: An artifact created in the workspace is explicitly marked as the deliverable and its durable event reaches the real web client.

scenarios.name: present_workspace_file
scenarios.summary: A workspace file is explicitly marked as the deliverable and opens in the sandboxed file viewer.

scenarios.name: preset_locked_denies_exec
scenarios.summary: The `locked` preset resolves to plan mode, so the model's shell call is denied before the executor is reached.

scenarios.name: read_then_edit_kernel
scenarios.summary: view_file then edit_file (SEARCH/REPLACE); the file changes on disk, the model sees the tool results, a diff card is emitted.

scenarios.name: read_then_edit_web_dom
scenarios.summary: Edit through the real client — view_file then edit_file; the diff card renders in the timeline, the file changes on disk, and the conversation survives a page refresh.

scenarios.name: restore_turn
scenarios.summary: The model writes a file, the user explicitly approves a turn-start restore, and the workspace returns to its original state.

scenarios.name: runaway_tool_loop_kernel
scenarios.summary: The model keeps calling the same tool; the kernel's iteration guard must end the turn and say so — and the replay must not be silently padded.

scenarios.name: sandbox_bwrap_full_badge
scenarios.summary: On a Linux host whose bubblewrap probe succeeds, the Studio labels the resolved standard preset with the verified backend enforcement.

scenarios.name: sandbox_unavailable_required_denies
scenarios.summary: Even explicit permission bypass cannot make required mode run an executor unconfined when the selected backend is unavailable.

scenarios.name: secret_redacted_from_model_kernel
scenarios.summary: Secrets guardrail — a value from the Secrets store and a well-known API-key pattern inside a file are redacted from the tool output before the model (and the transcript) sees it.

scenarios.name: security_preset_badge_web_dom
scenarios.summary: The Studio status chip shows the resolved preset and backend probe result from the kernel, not a browser-side default.

scenarios.name: session_reload_web_dom
scenarios.summary: Two turns through the real client, then a page refresh — the conversation must be visible again without any further click.

scenarios.name: session_resume_web
scenarios.summary: Two turns over HTTP with the browser's payload shape, then sessions.get — the history a page refresh would render must contain both turns.

scenarios.name: shell_exec_denied_without_approver_kernel
scenarios.summary: run_command (EXEC) in ask mode with no approver listening — fails closed, the command never runs, the model is told.

scenarios.name: skills_view_kernel
scenarios.summary: Progressive skills — the skills catalog is injected into the prompt and view_skill returns the full SKILL.md to the model (and a card to the UI).

scenarios.name: thinking_then_answer_web
scenarios.summary: Thinking deltas reach the client as model.thinking.delta; the final text is rendered; thinking is not fed back to the model as assistant text.

scenarios.name: tirith_blocks_ssrf_kernel
scenarios.summary: Tirith guardrail — a shell command targeting the cloud metadata endpoint is denied by policy even in allow mode; the model is told.

scenarios.name: tirith_blocks_ssrf_web_dom
scenarios.summary: A policy denial seen through the real client — the tool card must show DENIED with the reason, and the turn completes with the model's explanation.

scenarios.name: turn_changes_summary
scenarios.summary: A real browser turn edits two files, persists one bounded workspace summary, and advertises the Diffs panel.

settings.title: Maximum bytes returned for one on-demand file diff.
Maximum changed-file rows shown in one turn summary.
Skip checkpoint snapshots when Git-visible workspace files exceed this size; a system notice is recorded.
'block' refuses the call, 'warn' appends a note, 'off' keeps the guard loaded but idle.
Tools whose use counts as having read the file.
Block the call from this many identical calls; 0 never blocks.
Count identical tool calls within a turn.
Tools that are expected to be polled or paged.
Nag from this many identical calls in one turn.
Prune oversized tool results when the final result is built.
Tools whose output is already an explicit, ranged read.
Characters kept from the start, snapped to a line boundary.
Characters kept from the end, where test failures and stack traces are.
Results up to this length pass through untouched.
Copy oversized tool results into the session directory.
Tools whose results are never spilled (they are already paginated).
Cap on spool files kept per session; older ones are deleted.
Only results longer than this many characters are spilled.
Maximum retained jobs per session; oldest exited jobs are pruned before a new job starts.
In-memory output tail retained per job before reading the session spill file.
Maximum bytes retained in each session-scoped job output spill file.

tools.description: Ask the user up to 4 short multiple-choice questions when a decision materially changes what you will build. Prefer sensible defaults over asking; never ask what you can find out from the workspace.

tools.description: Restores the workspace to a previous shadow checkpoint. This is destructive and requires user approval. Use checkpoint_id 'turn-start' to restore to the beginning of the current turn.
tools.name: checkpoint_restore

tools.description: Creates a rich document or generative UI artifact with user-facing metadata.
tools.name: create_artifact

tools.description: Applies surgical SEARCH/REPLACE diff blocks to an existing file in the workspace.
tools.name: edit_file

tools.description: Stops a running background job. This is an execution action and follows normal approval policy.
tools.name: job_kill

tools.description: Lists jobs belonging to the current session, including running and recently exited jobs.
tools.name: job_list

tools.description: Reads a job's recent output or output bytes after a durable offset.
tools.name: job_output

tools.description: Starts a background process as a durable session job. Its output is spooled and survives the turn.
tools.name: job_start

tools.description: Deprecated compatibility alias for the durable job tools (retained for one minor version): query, wait, kill, or send stdin input.
tools.name: manage_task

tools.description: Mark an existing workspace file or artifact as a deliverable for the user and open it in the viewer. Use this when you finish producing the document, image, or result the user asked for.
tools.name: present

tools.description: Reads content from an external Model Context Protocol resource URI.
tools.name: read_resource

tools.description: Stores a persistent fact, preference, or architectural decision across sessions.
tools.name: remember

tools.description: Runs a shell command in the workspace via the executor with real-time output streaming and background transition.
tools.name: run_command

tools.description: Searches regular workspace files using regex matching without following symlinks.
tools.name: search_codebase

tools.description: Searches remembered facts and previous session turns/transcripts using full-text search.
tools.name: search_memory

tools.description: Reads and displays the contents of a file in the workspace with optional line ranges.
tools.name: view_file

tools.description: Loads and displays the complete playbook instructions and methodology for a specialized skill.
tools.name: view_skill

tools.description: Creates a new file or completely overwrites an existing file in the workspace.
tools.name: write_to_file
